claims.claim_vi: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses so users can reach websites by their human-readable names.

claims.claim_vi: A proxy server is an intermediary gateway between clients and other servers, providing additional security, performance optimization and anonymity.
claims.verified_by: Source body read from the pinned commit; the statement is in the source text.

claims.claim_vi: An origin server hosts the central source of content that is cached and distributed to edge servers for faster delivery to end users.

claims.claim_vi: The six types are roles, not six kinds of machine: one machine may take several roles and one role may be shared by several machines.

claims.claim_vi: Typical order of events for a page load: the browser asks DNS first, then reaches the web server, possibly through a proxy.

design_notes_vi: Sáu thẻ chia hai nhóm: ba loại đưa nội dung tới người dùng và ba loại dịch vụ nền của mạng. Không có mũi tên vì nguồn không nói thứ tự giữa các loại. Không dùng ảnh nguồn.
source_deviations: Source lists the six types in one flat order (web, mail, DNS, proxy, FTP, origin) without relating them; the lesson groups them into two sets of three and adds that they are roles rather than machines.
